vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: baoyu-post-to-weibo
Version: 1.69.1

The skill automates Weibo posting via Chrome CDP and utilizes high-risk system-level capabilities. It executes shell commands across multiple platforms (PowerShell, AppleScript, xclip/xdotool) in 'copy-to-clipboard.ts' and 'paste-from-clipboard.ts' to manipulate the system clipboard and simulate keystrokes. Furthermore, 'scripts/vendor/baoyu-md/src/utils/languages.ts' dynamically fetches and executes JavaScript from a remote CDN (cdn-doocs.oss-cn-shenzhen.aliyuncs.com) to load syntax highlighting grammars. While these behaviors are plausibly aligned with the stated goal of bypassing anti-bot measures and rendering Markdown, the combination of shell execution, system-wide automation, and remote code loading represents a significant attack surface.

llm.summary: The skill appears to do what it claims (drive a real Chrome instance to publish posts/articles to Weibo) and its code + runtime instructions are coherent with that purpose, but it performs sensitive local actions (reads Chrome profiles, manipulates clipboard, sends real keystrokes, and may kill Chrome CDP processes) that you should be aware of before running.

dimensions.detail: Name/description match the code and runtime instructions: scripts implement regular posts and headline articles via Chrome CDP, markdown-to-HTML conversion, clipboard helpers, and paste helpers. Required binaries (bun or npx) are reasonable for executing the provided TypeScript scripts.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs the agent to run local scripts from the scripts/ folder and to reuse or open Chrome profiles and CDP ports. The instructions explicitly suggest killing existing Chrome CDP instances automatically when the debug port isn't ready and to operate on Chrome user-data dirs; these are within the goal of driving a real browser but are sensitive actions (terminating browser processes, activating apps, performing real paste keystrokes, reading/writing profile files).
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No external install spec; skill is instruction/script-based and ships vendored dependencies. Nothing is downloaded at runtime from obscure URLs. Execution relies on local runtimes/tools (bun/npx, osascript/xdotool/powershell/etc.) which is expected for this approach.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The registry metadata declares no required env vars, but the code honors optional env overrides (e.g., BAOYU_CHROME_PATH, BAOYU_SHARED_PROFILE) and probes standard Chrome user-data dirs under the user's home. That access is coherent with reusing an existing logged-in Chrome session, but it means the skill will read (and potentially reuse) browser profile data beyond what the manifest declares.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false and no install step that makes the skill persistently active. The skill may reuse or launch Chrome with a remote-debugging port and will operate on existing browser profiles, but it does not modify other skills or request system-wide privileges in its metadata.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to be what it claims, but it performs sensitive local actions to bypass anti-bot defenses: it reads Chrome user-data directories, may start or reuse Chrome with a remote-debugging port, sends real paste keystrokes (osascript/xdotool/powershell), manipulates the system clipboard, and its troubleshooting guidance suggests killing existing Chrome/CDP processes automatically. Before installing/running: 1) Review the scripts (weibo-article.ts / weibo-post.ts) yourself; 2) Prefer running with a dedicated or disposable Chrome profile (use --profile) instead of your main profile to avoid leaking sessions or affecting other tabs; 3) Back up important Chrome profile data in case processes are killed or files are read; 4) Be aware the skill will spawn platform commands (swift, osascript, xdotool, powershell, etc.); 5) If you want extra safety, run the skill in an isolated environment (VM/container) or manually step through the commands rather than allowing full automation.
